config.title: Berlin to Prague - FAQ
config.subtitle: How long the train really takes, why Mondays are the wrong day to travel in 2026, what a ticket costs, and whether Prague works as a day trip from Berlin.

items.q: How long does the train from Berlin to Prague take?
items.a: **Just under four hours.** Almost every direct EuroCity covers Berlin Hauptbahnhof to Praha hlavni nadrazi in 3 hours 57 minutes, and only the last departure of the day stretches to a little over four hours. There are seven direct southbound trains, leaving roughly every two hours from 07:28 to 19:28, and six back from Prague between 06:31 and 16:31.

items.q: Is there a direct flight from Berlin to Prague?
items.a: **No.** Prague Airport has nonstop flights to 185 destinations in 63 countries and Berlin is not one of them. The cities are too close for anyone to sell a scheduled hop between them, so every flight result is a connection through somewhere like Frankfurt, Munich, Vienna or Warsaw. Once you add the trip out to BER, security, the layover and the ride in from Prague airport, none of them beats the train.

items.q: Why are Berlin to Prague trains cancelled on Mondays?
items.a: **Because of engineering work on the German side of the border, between Schöna and Bad Schandau.** On Mondays until 12 December 2026 buses replace trains between Dresden and Ústí nad Labem, the through service is split in two and Bad Schandau is skipped. Only the 17:28 and 19:28 out of Berlin and the 06:31 out of Prague survive, so there is no Monday morning departure and no Monday evening train home. On a Monday, take the bus or move the trip.

items.q: How much is a Berlin to Prague train ticket?
items.a: **Advance fares start at 18.99 euro in second class, and the fully flexible walk-up fare is 80 to 95 euro.** Booking opens up to six months ahead, and dates after the mid-December timetable change usually go on sale in mid-October. Buy at int.bahn.de, which charges no booking fee, or directly from Czech Railways. A seat reservation is optional most of the year and compulsory from mid-June to late August.

items.q: Is the bus from Berlin to Prague better than the train?
items.a: **It is a serious option rather than a fallback.** FlixBus lists around 25 departures a day with a fastest scheduled run of 3 hours 40 minutes, which is quicker than any train on the line, and RegioJet runs the same corridor from Berlin Südkreuz. Two things to weigh: the bus arrives at Florenc, two metro stops out from the old town, while the train puts you a ten-minute walk from Wenceslas Square, and an advance train ticket at 18.99 euro is already bus money. Where the bus wins outright is Monday, when the railway is cut and the motorway is not.

items.q: Can you do Prague as a day trip from Berlin?
items.a: **You can, but the numbers are poor.** The best pairing the timetable allows is out on the 07:28, into Prague at 11:25, back on the 16:31 and into Berlin at 20:29. That is 7 hours 55 minutes on a train for 5 hours 6 minutes in the city, and the last of those hours goes on walking back to the station. My advice is to give Prague one night: the same two tickets then buy you an evening and a morning, which is when the old town is actually worth being in. If you want a genuine day trip out of Berlin, Szczecin and Dresden are built for it.

items.q: Do you need a passport to travel from Berlin to Prague?
items.a: **Carry your passport or national ID card.** Both countries are in the Schengen area, but Germany has notified the European Commission of controls at all nine of its land borders, Czechia included, and the current notified period runs to 15 March 2027. On this line a check is usually a walk through the carriage, but it does happen. Remember also that Czechia uses the koruna and not the euro, and when a card terminal offers to charge you in euros, decline it and pay in koruna.
